title: WHERE A BATTERY'S DAY SWINGS MOST
subtitle: ERCOT's 195 storage nodes by their day-ahead intraday swing, the four dearest hours less the four cheapest, 2025-10 to 2026-09

inputs_words.min_days: at least 90 percent of the 335 days the table holds, of 365

chart.x_label: Mean intraday swing, USD per MWh: each bar from its label to 10 more

callouts.label: Mean intraday swing, USD per MWh, narrowest and widest
The middle storage node, USD per MWh
PALACIOS_RN, one day in ten and nine in ten, USD per MWh

why: On a mean day from 2025-10 to 2026-09, the four dearest day-ahead hours at ERCOT's storage nodes cost USD 34.22 (MOORE_FL_RN) to USD 105.86 (PALACIOS_RN) per MWh more than the four cheapest, with a median of USD 49.31 across the 195 storage nodes that hold at least 90 percent of the days. At PALACIOS_RN one day in ten swung USD 20.04 or less and one in ten USD 85.57 or more; its mean is above its 90th percentile, so a few days' swing carries it. The swing is a day's spread of prices at the node, not a battery's earnings: it leaves out losses, cycling and the ancillary markets.
footnote: Data: the All grids tab of "What a datacenter pays" (/cost-of-power?view=allgrids&rows=nodes&ncls=storage&nsort=swing&ndir=desc), from node_basis_daily's dam_spread_4h (each day's four dearest day-ahead hours' mean less its four cheapest), by site/data/siting/nodes.json. node_basis_daily lacks 2026-08-21 to 2026-09-19 for every node. Method: docs/methods/siting.md (decision 24).
source_line: Source: ERW, the All grids tab's node list (/cost-of-power?view=allgrids&rows=nodes), from ERCOT's day-ahead settlement point prices as node_basis_daily holds them.

round.caveat: Many claims were tested in this round; a claim's q-value is the false discovery rate at which it would still be kept over all of them (Benjamini and Hochberg). A caveat, not a test the card had to pass.
